title_o: Washing Away Your Sins: Threatened Morality and Physical Cleansing

replications.quote: We were unsuccessful in replicating the Zhong & Liljenquist ́s results that supported cleansing as a psychological mechanism for compensating guilty: results couldn’t confirm an increased mental accessibility of cleansing-related concepts or even a greater desire for cleansing products, neither a greater likelihood of taking antiseptic wipes. || We were unsuccessful in replicating the Zhong & Liljenquist's results that supported cleansing as a psychological mechanism for compensating guilty: results couldn't confirm an increased mental accessibility of cleansing-related concepts or even a greater desire for cleansing products, neither a greater likelihood of taking antiseptic wipes. In addition we didn't find that physical cleansing alleviates the upsetting consequences of unethical behaviour. || We were unsuccessful in replicating the Zhong & Liljenquist's results that supported cleansing as a psychological mechanism for compensating guilty: results couldn't confirm an increased mental accessibility of cleansing-related concepts or even a greater desire for cleansing products, neither a greater likelihood of taking antiseptic wipes.
Despite multiple good-faith efforts, however, we were unable to detect a “Macbeth Effect” in any of our experiments.

replications.journal: Advances in Methods and Practices in Psychological Science
replications.quote: This result is not consistent with the hypothesis that copying an account of an unethical action increases the desirability of cleans- ing products compared with copying an account of an ethical action.
